_comment: Pronunciation lexicon for Video K (narration skill, PRONUNCIATION.md). Only respell and accept change narration; say/ipa/lang/sources/decoy/note/probe are the record. Names and terms the script speaks (script.tsv of 63291ba): Tacoma, Schroeder, Wallace Sabine, eigenvalue(s), eigenvector(s), Eigen; London, Boston and Wallace are ordinary English and not listed. The brief's other names (Leontief, Helmholtz, Perron, Frobenius, Hilbert, Lanczos, Eigentöne) are not spoken in this script: add them if a revision speaks them. eigenvalue copied from Video J's record; the rest looked up and corrected by hand where the tool guessed, each note says how. Probed with probe_names.py run --voice michael on 2026-10-13; each probe.verdict says what the ASR heard. The owner's pronunciation overrides every entry. Narration triage of 2026-10-14 (R2 script, michael): 'accept' lists the American spellings the ASR writes for the script's British ones and the unit's abbreviation, each heard right in its take alone (02_4.1 neighbours, 05_2.1 millimetre, 09_4.2 metres, 10_3.0 and 11_3.0 hertz as Hz); 'phrases' maps 'at hum' to 'but hum' (09_5.2: the take alone is heard 'but hum', and so are cuts of the assembled line from 4.3 s and from 5.12 s; from 5.0 s it is heard 'At hum'; the take's first 0.9 s sits inside the line at correlation 0.9998, so the onset is whole and the miss is the ASR's window).

eigenvalue.note: Copied from Video J's lexicon (same voice and ftts build). Its probe: the plain word is heard right mid-sentence and at the end, and as 'Egin value' at a sentence start; this script never opens a sentence with it (03_6, 04_3, 12_4, 12_5, 13_4, 13_7, 14_3).

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: PARTIAL, as in Video J: the plain word heard as eigenvalue at the start and end carriers and as 'Egin value' in the middle one; EYE-gen-val-yoo was read as letters (iiGen, I Gen); the decoy EE-jen-value heard differently. Check the narration sheets of its lines.

eigenvector.note: The lookup tool returned the Dutch IPA; the English is EYE-gen. Spoken at 03_6, 06_2, 11_5, 12_4.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: PARTIAL: the plain word heard as eigenvector 2/3 ('Egon Vector' once, mid-sentence); EYE-gen-vek-ter was read as letters (iGen Vector); the decoy heard differently.

Eigen.note: German 'own'. 03_6 opens a sentence with it ('Eigen is German for own.'), the position where 'eigenvalue' failed in Video J's probe, so it is probed on its own.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: Plain word: heard as Eigen 3/3, including at a sentence start (the position 03_6 uses); EYE-gen was heard as iGen. The tool says UNVERIFIED because a plain spelling heard as itself proves nothing about the vowel, but the decoy EE-jen was heard differently (EEGEN, E.E. Jen).

Schroeder.note: Manfred Schroeder (German-born, at Bell Labs in the US for decades); German Schröder [ˈʃʁøːdɐ]. SHROH-der is the usual American reading of this spelling; no source gives his own usage, and the lookup tool returned Portuguese readings. Partial, for the owner's ear. Spoken at 10_6.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: PASS: the plain spelling heard as Schroeder 3/3 and the decoy SHRAY-der as Schrader 2/3, so the read is not SHRAY-der; SHROH-der as a respelling was garbled (Roshta). Still for the owner's ear (no source for his own usage).

Sabine.note: Wallace Clement Sabine. Wiktionary's General American reading of the name is SAY-bine; the unit named after him, the sabin, is SAY-bin in Merriam-Webster. No source gives the physicist's own usage: partial, for the owner's ear. Spoken at 11_1 ('Wallace Sabine').

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: PASS: SAY-bine heard as Sabine 3/3; SAY-bin heard as Sabin 3/3 (the unit's reading, kept as the alternative for the owner); the decoy suh-BEEN heard differently. For the owner's ear.

Tacoma.note: The Tacoma Narrows Bridge, 1940. Spoken at 08_1.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy (probe_names.py run)
probe.verdict: PASS: the plain word heard as Tacoma 3/3; tuh-KOH-muh as a respelling was garbled.
